scores.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Paul Tol palette, clean legend, and the collapsed-node count badges (+37, +16) are an elegant UX touch, but the lower half of the viewport is wasted empty space and the Phylum-level nodes render leaf-style (solid pink dots) when they should read as interior nodes, muddying the depth encoding.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: No quantitative encodings to deceive — tree is structurally honest with data-driven layout, accurate descendant counts, and categorical color/size; minor robustness risk from non-unique key (name+depth) that could corrupt joins if sibling names collide.
scores.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() call before starting new transitions in update(), so rapid node clicks or expand-all during a 500ms transition will cause jumping/snapping; search is properly debounced (200ms), no brush/zoom means Update Storm and Stale Scale are N/A, and pointer events unify mouse/touch correctly.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Clean progressive disclosure with 6 rank colors, collapsed counts, and search highlighting keeps a 200-node taxonomy manageable at every expansion level; static screenshot shows only 12 visible nodes with clear hierarchy and no label overlap.

proposer: 548 lines, down 5 from 553. Inlined `treeHeight`, `treeWidth`, and `transitionDur` variables that were each used only once, and simplified the `snap` helper by removing the intermediate object.
